name: 19th Annual Suwannee River Wilderness Trail
startLoc: Madison Blue Spring State Park, Lee
included: Camping, catered breakfasts and dinners, daily lunch snacks and evening programs.
cabinsNote: Rentals: Suwannee River Canoe Outpost (official outfitter), 386-364-4991.

overview.title: Our classic Suwannee journey
overview.text: Six days down the Suwannee River, from Madison Blue Spring to Branford, through springs, state parks and river camps with screened platforms, fans, electricity and hot showers.
minis: Longest day, with a springs lunch stop
Screened platforms, fans, power and hot showers

days.title: Arrive and settle in
days.body: Check in at Suwannee River State Park, then dinner, an evening program and the required trip orientation.

days.title: Madison Blue Spring to Suwannee River State Park
days.body: Launch at Madison Blue Spring State Park and paddle 12 miles to Suwannee River State Park.

days.title: To Dowling Park River Camp
days.body: Fifteen miles to Dowling Park River Camp, with screened platforms, fans, electricity and hot showers.

days.title: To Lafayette Blue Springs State Park
days.body: A shorter 10-mile day ending at Lafayette Blue Springs State Park.

days.title: A day of springs to Adams Tract
days.lunch: Peacock Slough River Camp, about 8.5 miles in
days.body: The longest day, 18 miles with a lunch stop at Peacock Slough River Camp, and a night at Adams Tract River Camp.

days.title: The final stretch to Branford
days.body: The last miles to Ivey Memorial Park in Branford, with a rest stop at Little River Springs.

boat: Sit-in kayak, sit-on-top kayak or paddleboard, at least 12 feet. Beginners are welcome, with basic paddling and swimming skills.
water: Non-inflatable Coast Guard-approved PFD, worn on the water
Bow line, 8 to 10 ft, secured so it cannot come loose
Grab loops at bow and stern
First aid kit in a waterproof cover
Repair kit (duct tape, sealant, waterproof tape)
Rain gear and a fleece or light jacket
Dry change of clothes in a waterproof bag
Water for the day and snacks (lunch is provided)
land: Something to read, music or earplugs
faq: Dinner at 6 PM and an evening program at 7 PM. Programs include authors, historians and environmental experts, and one night of live music.
Yes. Pre-trip and post-trip shuttle options are available. Check your confirmation email for times. One option involves being at the Shrine Club in Branford by 1 PM on March 20.
Open to all skill levels. Paddlers under 18 must be with a parent or guardian, with no more than two children under 12 per adult. A signed waiver and emergency contact are required. No pets.
What are the rules on the water?
Wear a non-inflatable PFD at all times. People-powered boats only. Follow park rules, including the alcohol ban, and respect private property along the river.
All payments are non-refundable, including for weather and water levels. Paddle Florida strongly recommends buying trip cancellation insurance from an outside provider.
Yes. Final details are emailed 7 to 10 days before the trip.
